mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which lowers borrowing costs and increases consumer and business spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by 10 basis points in the last month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreased by 10 basis points.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of instances where UNRATE increased by 0.2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate increased demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of instances where HOUST increased by 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production suggests strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of instances where INDPRO increased by 1%.

mechanism_narrative: Low inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of instances where PAYEMS increased by 1%.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of instances where RSAFS increased by 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5%, it indicates tight monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%.
